notesDetails.title: Why './cb https://rizafahmi.com' Failed With 33 'Unknown CA' Alerts: Misreading Truncated ExUnit Output at Line 125 Wiped All 160 System CA Certs
bullets: Holdout Verdict vs. Repo PLAN.md (4/7 vs. 7/7 Checked): Although the agent checked [x] on S1–S7 in PLAN.md and passed 46/46 local ExUnit tests (27.2s), live verification against ./cb https://rizafahmi.com fails all 33 requests with Transport failures: 33 ({:tls, {:tls_alert, {:unknown_ca, ...}}}), reports HTTP responses: 0 and Latency (HTTP responses): p50 n/a, p95 n/a with exit code 1, and dumps 33 OTP =NOTICE REPORT==== TLS alert blocks onto stdout (failing S5–S7 holdout checks while ./cb http://rizafahmi.com passes with 45/45 301 responses).

How Line 125 Introduced the Bug After Line 100 Was Already Correct: When writing lib/capy_bench/http.ex on Turn 41 (Line 100), the agent originally wrote defp system_cacerts, do: :public_key.cacerts_get()—which works natively on OTP 28. However, at Line 124, a KeyError in test/support/http_server.ex printed a failed assertion showing the %CapyBench.HTTP{} struct with truncated cacerts: [{:cert, <<48, 130, ...>>, ...}, ...]. At Line 125 (08:26:55 WIB), the agent misread that truncated 3-tuple #cert{} record ({:cert, der, otp_cert}) as a 2-tuple {:cert, der} and added normalize_cacerts/1 matching {:cert, der} when is_binary(der) -> [der] and _ -> []—silently filtering all 160 macOS system CA certificates to [] whenever SSL_CERT_FILE is unset.

Why Local HTTPS Tests & Release Verification Missed Both Bugs: Every trusted HTTPS test in test/capy_bench/cli_http_test.exs and /tmp/capy_release_check.py injected SSL_CERT_FILE=_build/test/certs/ca.pem (bypassing system_cacerts/0 for load_pem_cacerts/1), while the untrusted HTTPS test (SSL_CERT_FILE=nil) expected :unknown_ca and passed for the wrong reason because cacerts: [] rejects every certificate. Furthermore, the agent added log_level: :none to :ssl.listen in test/support/http_server.ex (Line 148) to silence test output, but never added log_level: :none to :ssl.connect in lib/capy_bench/http.ex, leaving client TLS alerts routed to stdout.

notesDetails.title: S1 Signal-Probing Timeouts (110.1s / 24.1% of Tool Time) & the '+B i' + SIGUSR2 Wrapper Architecture (Exit 159 Race in S7)
bullets: Inspecting Nix Store system.ex & Three Probe Timeouts (Lines 41–69): After System.trap_signal(:sigint, ...) failed in /tmp/cb_probe.exs (Line 41–42), the agent inspected /nix/store/.../elixir-1.20.4/lib/elixir/lib/elixir/lib/system.ex at Line 56–57 and confirmed @signals excludes :sigint. Its next three probes hit sequential timeouts totaling 110.1s (24.1% of all tool time): sending \003 to raw elixir /tmp/sleep_probe.exs opened the BEAM BREAK: (a)bort menu and timed out after 30.0s (Line 59); scanning /nix/store for erl.xml timed out after 20.0s (Line 63); and iterating over '+B', '+B c', '+B d', '+B i' in expect hung on '+B c' for 60.1s (Line 65) and left an erl_crash.dump cleaned up at Line 85.

POSIX SIGUSR2 Wrapper & S7 Startup Race (Exit 159 vs. 130 at Line 178): Having proved at Line 69 that '+B i' ignores terminal SIGINT while keeping the VM alive, the agent built escript cb.escript with emu_args: "+B i" and committed a /bin/sh wrapper (cb) that traps INT and runs kill -USR2 "$child" toward System.trap_signal(:sigusr2, ...). In S7 (Line 178), sending Ctrl-C at 200ms in test/capy_bench/ctrl_c_test.exs failed with exit status 159 (128 + 31, default SIGUSR2 termination on macOS) because the signal arrived while the BEAM escript was still booting before CapyBench.CLI.main/1 registered the trap; increasing ctrl_c_after to 600ms–700ms (Line 179) resolved all 3 PTY tests.

notesDetails.title: Single-Turn 481-Line HTTP Client Synthesis (15,579 Output Tokens) & 14 Chained Inline Python File Patches
bullets: Two Mega-Turns Drove 24.2% of All Output Tokens: Turn 41 (Line 100, S3) synthesized the entire 481-line raw :gen_tcp/:ssl HTTP/1.1 client (lib/capy_bench/http.ex) in a single write call emitting 15,579 output tokens (11,554 reasoning tokens) in 86.2s ($0.0191), and Turn 56 (Line 131, S4) synthesized lib/capy_bench/benchmark.ex in a single write call emitting 9,442 output tokens (7,843 reasoning tokens) in 60.0s ($0.0121).

14 Chained python3 Path().replace() Bash Scripts (Lines 125–195): Starting in S3 (Line 125), the agent largely stopped calling Pi's edit tool and instead embedded python3 - <<'PY' file-patching scripts chained directly with mix format && mix test && git commit inside single bash calls. This compressed S5 (Lines 156–165), S6 (Lines 166–173), and S7 (Lines 174–184) into just 4, 4, and 5 LLM turns (~60s per slice), at the cost of one silent str.replace no-op at Line 144 when mix format had wrapped a target line in test/capy_bench/cli_http_test.exs.

Zero Dependencies (deps: []) & Post-Run Credo Audit: Like pi-muse-spark-1-3-contrib-high, the agent kept deps: [] empty and defined mix lint as ["format --check-formatted", "compile --force --warnings-as-errors"] rather than adding Credo (despite PLAN.md stating 'Formatting and compilation do not substitute for linting'). A post-run credo --strict check across all 14 files (74 mods/funs) found 0 issues in lib/ and only 1 nesting-depth refactoring opportunity in test/support/http_server.ex:152 (CapyBench.TestSupport.HTTPServer.parse_request).
